paragraphs.title: The Chief Butler and Baker Are Imprisoned

easy.question: Who offended the king of Egypt?
answers: The chief butler and the chief baker
Joseph and the captain of the guard
Pharaoh and two of his servants
easy.explanation: The verse says that the chief butler and chief baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.

easy.question: At whom was Pharaoh angry?
answers: Joseph alone
The chief butler and the chief baker
The captain of the guard
easy.explanation: Pharaoh was angry with his two officers: the chief butler and the chief baker.

easy.question: Where was Joseph when the two officers were brought to him?
answers: In Pharaoh’s house
In the chief butler’s house
In prison
easy.explanation: The passage states that Joseph was bound in prison.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: The officers offended Pharaoh, Pharaoh became angry, and they were put in prison
Joseph served the officers, and then they offended Pharaoh
Pharaoh released the officers and then sent them to Joseph
medium.explanation: First the officers offended Pharaoh, then he became angry with them, and finally he placed them in custody.

medium.question: What happened to the two officers according to the verse?
answers: They were celebrated at a feast
They were held under guard in prison
They were assigned kitchen work
medium.explanation: The context says they were kept in prison under guard.

medium.question: Who placed Joseph in charge of the two officers?
answers: Pharaoh
The chief butler
The captain of the guard
medium.explanation: The captain of the guard charged Joseph with serving the two officers.

challenge.question: Why does the passage emphasize that the prison was the place where Joseph was already bound?
answers: To explain why Joseph met the two officers there
To show that Joseph had already left prison
To teach that Pharaoh lived in the prison
challenge.explanation: The emphasis shows that the officers were brought to the same place where Joseph was already imprisoned, making their meeting possible.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Joseph serving the officers even though he was imprisoned?
answers: Joseph was king over Egypt
He was trusted with responsibility even as a prisoner
Joseph was one of the officers who had offended Pharaoh
challenge.explanation: Although Joseph was a prisoner, he was put in charge of the officers and served them, suggesting that he was trusted.

challenge.question: What do the titles “chief butler” and “chief baker” tell us about their duties?
answers: They guarded the prison
They were members of Pharaoh’s family
They supervised the drink and baking in the royal household
challenge.explanation: The titles identify them as officials responsible for the king’s drink and baked goods.

questions.question: Why does the passage emphasize that the prison was the place where Joseph was already bound?
answers: To explain why Joseph met the two officers there
To show that Joseph had already left prison
To teach that Pharaoh lived in the prison
questions.explanation: The emphasis shows that the officers were brought to the same place where Joseph was already imprisoned, making their meeting possible.

questions.question: What can we infer from Joseph serving the officers even though he was imprisoned?
answers: Joseph was king over Egypt
He was trusted with responsibility even as a prisoner
Joseph was one of the officers who had offended Pharaoh
questions.explanation: Although Joseph was a prisoner, he was put in charge of the officers and served them, suggesting that he was trusted.

questions.question: What do the titles “chief butler” and “chief baker” tell us about their duties?
answers: They guarded the prison
They were members of Pharaoh’s family
They supervised the drink and baking in the royal household
questions.explanation: The titles identify them as officials responsible for the king’s drink and baked goods.

paragraphs.title: The Officers’ Dreams and Joseph’s Concern for Them

easy.question: Who dreamed the dreams?
answers: The butler and the baker
Joseph and Pharaoh
The prison officials
easy.explanation: The passage says that the butler and baker of the king of Egypt dreamed dreams.

easy.question: When did Joseph come to the butler and baker?
answers: In the evening
In the morning
At midnight
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Joseph came in unto them in the morning.”

easy.question: What did the butler and baker tell Joseph?
answers: That they wanted to leave prison
That they were angry with Pharaoh
That they had dreamed and had no interpreter
easy.explanation: They told Joseph, “We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter of it.”

medium.question: Why did Joseph ask the butler and baker what was wrong?
answers: He saw that they were sad
He wanted to ask them for food
Pharaoh had sent him to examine them
medium.explanation: Joseph saw that they looked sad and asked why they looked so sadly that day.

medium.question: What did Joseph notice about the officers when he saw them in the morning?
answers: They were very hungry
They were sad
They were asleep
medium.explanation: The passage says that Joseph looked at them and saw that they were sad.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: Joseph interpreted the dream, and then they said they had dreamed
They told Joseph about the dream, then dreamed it, and finally Joseph saw them
They dreamed at night, Joseph saw them in the morning, and then they said they had no interpreter
medium.explanation: They dreamed at night; in the morning Joseph saw their sadness; after he asked them, they told him that they had no interpreter.

challenge.question: What can we learn from the phrase “each man his dream”?
answers: Each man had his own dream, not exactly the same dream
They both dreamed about Joseph
Only one of them really dreamed
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that each officer had a separate dream, even though both dreamed on the same night.

challenge.question: What does Joseph’s statement, “Do not interpretations belong to God?” reveal about his attitude?
answers: Joseph did not believe dreams could be interpreted
Joseph credited God, rather than himself alone, with interpreting dreams
Joseph thought only Pharaoh could interpret dreams
challenge.explanation: Joseph said that interpretations belong to God, showing faith and humility before hearing the dreams.

challenge.question: Why does the passage say that both men dreamed “in one night,” even though each had his own dream?
answers: To say that they dreamed exactly the same thing
To show that they slept in the same bed
To emphasize the timing connecting the dreams and their shared distress
challenge.explanation: The phrase connects the two dreams in time, while “each man his dream” makes clear that they were different dreams.

questions.question: What can we learn from the phrase “each man his dream”?
answers: Each man had his own dream, not exactly the same dream
They both dreamed about Joseph
Only one of them really dreamed
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that each officer had a separate dream, even though both dreamed on the same night.

questions.question: What does Joseph’s statement, “Do not interpretations belong to God?” reveal about his attitude?
answers: Joseph did not believe dreams could be interpreted
Joseph credited God, rather than himself alone, with interpreting dreams
Joseph thought only Pharaoh could interpret dreams
questions.explanation: Joseph said that interpretations belong to God, showing faith and humility before hearing the dreams.

questions.question: Why does the passage say that both men dreamed “in one night,” even though each had his own dream?
answers: To say that they dreamed exactly the same thing
To show that they slept in the same bed
To emphasize the timing connecting the dreams and their shared distress
questions.explanation: The phrase connects the two dreams in time, while “each man his dream” makes clear that they were different dreams.

paragraphs.title: The Chief Butler’s Dream and Its Interpretation

easy.question: What did the chief butler see in his dream?
answers: A vine
A palace
A horse
easy.explanation: The chief butler told Joseph, “Behold, a vine was before me.”

easy.question: How many branches were on the vine in the dream?
answers: Two
Three
Five
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And in the vine were three branches.”

easy.question: What did Joseph ask the chief butler to do when things went well for him?
answers: Bring him grapes
Tell him the dream
Mention him to Pharaoh
easy.explanation: Joseph asked him to mention him to Pharaoh so that Pharaoh might bring him out of prison.

medium.question: What did the chief butler do in the dream, in the correct order?
answers: He took grapes, pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and gave the cup to Pharaoh
He gave Pharaoh a vine and then took the cup
He drank the wine himself and returned the grapes
medium.explanation: He took the grapes, pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and then placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.

medium.question: According to the verse, what would happen to the chief butler within three days?
answers: He would receive a new cup
He would be restored to his former position
He would return to his own house
medium.explanation: Joseph said that Pharaoh would restore him to his place and that he would again serve Pharaoh’s cup.

medium.question: Why did Joseph ask the chief butler to remember him?
answers: He wanted the vine from the dream
He wanted to learn how to make wine
He hoped the butler would mention him to Pharaoh and help free him
medium.explanation: Joseph asked the butler to tell Pharaoh about him so that he could be brought out of prison.

challenge.question: What connection did Joseph make between the three branches and three days?
answers: The branches represented three days until the dream’s fulfillment
The branches represented three people in the palace
The branches represented three cups of wine
challenge.explanation: Joseph explicitly interpreted the three branches as three days.

challenge.question: What does “Pharaoh shall lift up thine head” mean according to the rest of the verse?
answers: Pharaoh would punish him immediately
Pharaoh would restore him to his former position
Pharaoh would send him to another country
challenge.explanation: The next words explain that Pharaoh would restore him to his place, meaning his former position.

challenge.question: How did Joseph describe his situation in verse 15 to persuade the chief butler to help him?
answers: He said he was from a royal family
He claimed to interpret every dream
He emphasized that he had been stolen from the land of the Hebrews and had done nothing deserving imprisonment
challenge.explanation: Joseph presented himself as unjustly treated: he had been taken from his land and imprisoned even though he had done nothing wrong.

questions.question: What connection did Joseph make between the three branches and three days?
answers: The branches represented three days until the dream’s fulfillment
The branches represented three people in the palace
The branches represented three cups of wine
questions.explanation: Joseph explicitly interpreted the three branches as three days.

questions.question: What does “Pharaoh shall lift up thine head” mean according to the rest of the verse?
answers: Pharaoh would punish him immediately
Pharaoh would restore him to his former position
Pharaoh would send him to another country
questions.explanation: The next words explain that Pharaoh would restore him to his place, meaning his former position.

questions.question: How did Joseph describe his situation in verse 15 to persuade the chief butler to help him?
answers: He said he was from a royal family
He claimed to interpret every dream
He emphasized that he had been stolen from the land of the Hebrews and had done nothing deserving imprisonment
questions.explanation: Joseph presented himself as unjustly treated: he had been taken from his land and imprisoned even though he had done nothing wrong.

paragraphs.title: The Chief Baker’s Dream and Its Troubling Interpretation

easy.question: Who told Joseph the dream described in these verses?
answers: The chief butler
The chief baker
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: The chief baker saw that Joseph had interpreted the first dream well and then told Joseph his own dream.

easy.question: How many baskets did the chief baker see in his dream?
answers: Three
Two
Four
easy.explanation: The chief baker saw three baskets on his head.

easy.question: Who ate the food from the upper basket?
answers: The chief baker
Pharaoh
The birds
easy.explanation: In the dream, the birds ate the food from the basket on the chief baker’s head.

medium.question: What did Joseph do when he interpreted the chief baker’s dream?
answers: He explained the meaning of the dream
He forgot the dream
He wrote down the dream
medium.explanation: Joseph gave an interpretation, explaining what the dream meant.

medium.question: Why did the chief baker tell Joseph his dream?
answers: He wanted to escape from prison
He saw that Joseph had interpreted the previous dream well
Pharaoh commanded him to tell it
medium.explanation: After hearing Joseph’s good interpretation of the chief butler’s dream, the chief baker asked Joseph to interpret his dream too.

medium.question: What connection did Joseph make between the three baskets and the chief baker’s future?
answers: The three baskets represented three days
The three baskets represented three people
The three baskets represented three meals
medium.explanation: Joseph explicitly said that the three baskets represented three days.

challenge.question: What does “Pharaoh shall lift up thy head from off thee” mean according to the rest of the verse?
answers: Pharaoh would honor the chief baker
Pharaoh would release the chief baker
Pharaoh would cause the chief baker’s death
challenge.explanation: The next words explain that the chief baker would be hanged on a tree, resulting in his death.

challenge.question: Which detail in the dream especially suggests that the chief baker’s food would not reach people?
answers: The baskets were on his head
The birds ate the food from the basket
There were three baskets
challenge.explanation: The birds eating the food shows that it was taken away instead of reaching those who would eat it.

challenge.question: Which sequence of events matches the passage?
answers: The chief baker dreamed, Joseph interpreted the dream, and a troubling event would happen within three days
Joseph dreamed, the chief baker interpreted it, and Pharaoh released him immediately
Pharaoh dreamed, the chief baker told Joseph, and Joseph prepared the food
challenge.explanation: First the chief baker told his dream, then Joseph interpreted it and announced what would happen three days later.

questions.question: What does “Pharaoh shall lift up thy head from off thee” mean according to the rest of the verse?
answers: Pharaoh would honor the chief baker
Pharaoh would release the chief baker
Pharaoh would cause the chief baker’s death
questions.explanation: The next words explain that the chief baker would be hanged on a tree, resulting in his death.

questions.question: Which detail in the dream especially suggests that the chief baker’s food would not reach people?
answers: The baskets were on his head
The birds ate the food from the basket
There were three baskets
questions.explanation: The birds eating the food shows that it was taken away instead of reaching those who would eat it.

questions.question: Which sequence of events matches the passage?
answers: The chief baker dreamed, Joseph interpreted the dream, and a troubling event would happen within three days
Joseph dreamed, the chief baker interpreted it, and Pharaoh released him immediately
Pharaoh dreamed, the chief baker told Joseph, and Joseph prepared the food
questions.explanation: First the chief baker told his dream, then Joseph interpreted it and announced what would happen three days later.

paragraphs.title: Pharaoh’s Birthday and the Fulfillment of the Interpretations

easy.question: What did Pharaoh do on his birthday?
answers: He held a feast for his servants
He went to war
He built a palace
easy.explanation: The verse says that Pharaoh made a feast for all his servants on his birthday.

easy.question: What position did the chief butler receive again?
answers: Chief baker
Serving Pharaoh’s cup
Overseeing the palace
easy.explanation: Pharaoh restored the chief butler to his position, and he placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.

easy.question: What did Pharaoh do to the chief baker?
answers: He released him
He restored him to his position
He hanged him
easy.explanation: The passage says that Pharaoh hanged the chief baker.

medium.question: What was the difference between the fates of the chief butler and the chief baker?
answers: The chief butler was restored to his position, but the chief baker was hanged
Both were restored to their positions
Both were hanged
medium.explanation: Pharaoh restored the chief butler, but hanged the chief baker, just as Joseph had interpreted.

medium.question: What happened when Pharaoh “lifted up the heads” of the two officers?
answers: He immediately honored both men
He brought both men before him and then determined their fates
He returned both men to their former jobs
medium.explanation: Pharaoh brought both officers before him at the feast, but their outcomes were different.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: The chief baker was hanged, and then the feast was held
Joseph interpreted the dreams, and then the two officers were born
The feast was held, Pharaoh brought the officers before him, and their fates were decided
medium.explanation: First came the feast, then Pharaoh brought the two officers before him, and finally the interpretations were fulfilled.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that the two officers were brought “among his servants”?
answers: The event took place in the royal court before Pharaoh’s attendants
The officers were members of Pharaoh’s family
The officers permanently left their jobs
challenge.explanation: The phrase places the event in the royal setting, among Pharaoh’s servants and attendants.

challenge.question: What does the use of the same expression, “lifted up the head,” for both officers show, even though their fates differed?
answers: They both received equal honor
Both were brought before Pharaoh, but the expression did not determine the outcome of their judgment
Both returned to their former jobs
challenge.explanation: The same expression describes bringing both officers before Pharaoh, but one was restored and the other was hanged.

challenge.question: Why was Pharaoh’s birthday an appropriate time for Joseph’s interpretations to be fulfilled?
answers: Joseph left prison on that day
The chief baker prepared a cake that day
It was a royal event at which Pharaoh could examine and decide the fate of his servants
challenge.explanation: The feast and gathering of Pharaoh’s servants created an occasion for Pharaoh to decide the officers’ cases.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that the two officers were brought “among his servants”?
answers: The event took place in the royal court before Pharaoh’s attendants
The officers were members of Pharaoh’s family
The officers permanently left their jobs
questions.explanation: The phrase places the event in the royal setting, among Pharaoh’s servants and attendants.

Both returned to their former jobs
questions.explanation: The same expression describes bringing both officers before Pharaoh, but one was restored and the other was hanged.

answers: Joseph left prison on that day

questions.explanation: The feast and gathering of Pharaoh’s servants created an occasion for Pharaoh to decide the officers’ cases.

easy.question: Who did not remember Joseph?
answers: The chief butler
The chief baker
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: The verse says that the chief butler did not remember Joseph.

easy.question: What did the chief butler do regarding Joseph?
answers: He released him
He forgot him
He called him before Pharaoh
easy.explanation: The verse says that the chief butler forgot Joseph.

easy.question: What was Joseph’s situation after the chief butler forgot him?
answers: He became an official
He left prison
He remained forgotten
easy.explanation: Because the chief butler forgot him, Joseph remained in prison and was not brought to Pharaoh’s attention.

medium.question: What is the relationship between “did not remember Joseph” and “forgot him”?
answers: Both statements emphasize that the chief butler forgot Joseph
The first says Joseph remembered, while the second says the butler remembered
The first describes a dream, while the second describes an interpretation
medium.explanation: Both expressions repeat and reinforce the fact that the chief butler forgot Joseph.

medium.question: What was the result of the chief butler forgetting Joseph?
answers: Joseph received a new position
Joseph became king
Joseph remained without anyone mentioning him to Pharaoh
medium.explanation: Since the chief butler forgot Joseph, Joseph remained in prison without being mentioned to Pharaoh.

medium.question: What can we infer about the help Joseph expected from the chief butler?
answers: It was given immediately
It was unnecessary
It did not come at that time
medium.explanation: The chief butler’s failure to remember Joseph shows that the expected help did not come at that time.

challenge.question: Why does the passage say both that the chief butler did not remember Joseph and that he forgot him?
answers: To emphasize the extent of his forgetfulness
To say that two different people forgot Joseph
To describe two different dreams
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording emphasizes that the chief butler completely failed to remember Joseph or mention him.

challenge.question: What happened because the chief butler forgot Joseph?
answers: Joseph was brought before Pharaoh
Joseph remained in prison
Joseph was appointed chief baker
challenge.explanation: The immediate result was that Joseph continued to be forgotten and remained in prison.

challenge.question: What does the final verse suggest about Joseph’s situation?
answers: His request for help was fulfilled immediately
His imprisonment no longer mattered
His hoped-for rescue was delayed
challenge.explanation: The chief butler’s forgetfulness shows that Joseph’s hoped-for rescue was delayed.

answers: To emphasize the extent of his forgetfulness

To describe two different dreams
questions.explanation: The repeated wording emphasizes that the chief butler completely failed to remember Joseph or mention him.
